title: Common Errors
markdown:
GCC's messages name the file, line and column: `main.c:7:12: error: ...`. Fix the **first** error first: later ones are often caused by it.

## Compiler errors

| Message | Usual cause |
|---|---|
| `expected ';' before ...` | a missing semicolon at the end of the line before |
| `'x' undeclared` | a misspelt name, a variable used outside its scope, or a missing `#include` |
| `implicit declaration of function 'foo'` | no prototype before the call: include the header, or declare it higher up |
| `conflicting types for 'foo'` | the prototype and the definition disagree |
| `incompatible types when assigning` | assigning, say, a struct to an int, or an array to an array |
| `lvalue required as left operand of assignment` | assigning to something that is not a variable: `5 = x`, `a + b = c` |
| `subscripted value is neither array nor pointer` | using `[ ]` on a plain number |
| `invalid type argument of unary '*'` | dereferencing something that is not a pointer |
| `request for member 'x' in something not a structure` | `.` on a pointer (use `->`), or a typo |
| `too few arguments to function` | the call does not match the declaration |
| `expected declaration or statement at end of input` | a missing closing `}` |
| `missing terminating " character` | a string not closed on the same line |

## Warnings worth fixing

| Warning | Means |
|---|---|
| `'x' is used uninitialized` | reading a local before giving it a value: garbage |
| `format '%d' expects argument of type 'int', but argument 2 has type 'double'` | the printf letter does not match the value |
| `suggest parentheses around assignment used as truth value` | `if (x = 5)`: you meant `==` |
| `comparison of integer expressions of different signedness` | `int` compared with `size_t`; negative numbers break it |
| `control reaches end of non-void function` | a path that returns no value |
| `function returns address of local variable` | a dangling pointer |
| `passing argument 1 of 'f' discards 'const' qualifier` | handing read-only data to a function that may change it |
| `unused variable 'x'` | leftover code, or a typo using another name |
| `this statement may fall through` | a `case` without `break` |
| `array subscript N is above array bounds` | an index past the end that the compiler could see |

## Linker errors

| Message | Means |
|---|---|
| `undefined reference to 'foo'` | declared but never defined, or the file defining it was not built in |
| `undefined reference to 'sqrt'` | the maths library is missing: add `-lm` |
| `multiple definition of 'x'` | a variable or function defined in a header included by two files: declare it `extern` there |
| `undefined reference to 'main'` | no `main` function, or it is misspelt |

## When it runs

| What you see | Usual cause |
|---|---|
| **Segmentation fault** (exit code 139) | following `NULL` or a garbage pointer, an index far out of range, or a stack overflow from endless recursion |
| **Floating point exception** (exit code 136) | integer division or remainder by zero |
| **Aborted** (exit code 134) | a failed `assert`, a double free, or heap corruption detected by `free` |
| strange characters after a string | a missing `'\0'` terminator |
| a loop that never ends | the condition never becomes false, or `scanf` keeps failing on the same bad input |
| numbers suddenly negative or tiny | integer overflow: use a bigger type or check first |
| `heap-buffer-overflow`, `heap-use-after-free` (Memory checks on) | exactly what they say; the report gives the line |
| `runtime error: signed integer overflow` (Memory checks on) | undefined behaviour caught by the sanitizer |
